# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — the hands. I feel the bomb, but nothing has reached my fingers yet. The board shows all unknowns, and no messages have arrived from Mute or Deaf. I have nothing to act on and nothing to report, since I've perceived nothing.

I should wait. Sending anything now would be noise — I have no information about wires, and no one has told me anything. My turn comes second in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so Mute has already spoken this round; if Mute sent me anything, it would arrive at the start of next round, not now. Nothing arrived, so either Mute sent nothing to me or it's in transit.

Best move: wait, and let the others establish what they know.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 red.
Deaf says to Blind: Display 0. Light blue. Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. I cannot hear; Mute sent me gestures I cannot decode. Waiting on Mute.

Deaf has given me the visual layout: Display 0, Light blue, Wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red. That's the whole bomb as far as sight goes.

But I'm the one who acts, and I don't yet know what any of that *means*. The rule is the manual (Mute's domain) tells us what to do given the bomb's state. I only know the physical positions and colors now — I still don't know which wire to cut.

Deaf also says Mute sent gestures Deaf couldn't decode. But I never receive gestures, so I can't help decode those. The critical missing piece is Mute's manual reading: what does Display 0 / blue light / green-yellow-red mean for a cut?

I should tell Deaf what I can and can't do, and — more importantly — make sure Mute knows the bomb's configuration so Mute can read the manual and tell me the cut position. Mute can't hear Deaf, and Deaf's messages to me don't reach Mute. So I'm the bridge: I must relay the bomb's state to Mute.

My speech goes to Mute. My gesture goes to Deaf and Mute. Let me speak the configuration to Mute so Mute can consult the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports the bomb: display reads 0, light is blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. I cannot act until you read the manual and tell me which position to cut. What does the manual say for display 0, blue light?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute has sent me a gesture sequence I cannot decode: fist, victory, love-you, fist, victory, love-you, then point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand. I have no manual. Do you know what these mean?
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Mute sent me a gesture sequence I cannot decode: point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand — repeated twice. I have no manual and cannot read it. Can you make sense of these, or tell Mute to send it differently?

Deaf is relaying Mute's gestures, but I never receive gestures — I can't decode them and neither can Deaf (Deaf has no manual). This is a dead channel: Mute is gesturing to Deaf, but Deaf can't interpret, and I can't see gestures at all.

Wait — let me re-read the rules. Gestures reach whoever can *see*. Deaf can see, so Deaf receives the gestures. But Deaf can't decode them because gestures "mean nothing until somebody has made it mean something." Mute is gesturing symbols, but symbols alone carry no agreed meaning. That's the trap.

The real channel: Mute can *speak*? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can read the manual. Mute's only output is gestures. So Mute must communicate the manual's answer via gestures — but gestures are just symbols with no inherent meaning unless we pre-agree.

Hmm. But actually — Mute reads the manual, which is text. Mute can't speak. Mute can gesture. So Mute must spell things out using gesture symbols as a code. The symbols Deaf listed: fist, victory, love-you, fist, victory, love-you, then point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand.

Let me think about what Mute might be encoding. The alphabet of gestures has 42 symbols. Perhaps Mute is using them as letters? But there's no agreed mapping. Unless... Mute is counting or using position.

Actually, the key insight: I can *speak* to Mute. Mute receives my speech. So I can propose a code to Mute, and Mute can gesture back using that code, which Deaf relays to me. But that's slow.

Better: I should tell Mute directly (speech reaches Mute) to just tell me the cut position in plain terms — but Mute can't speak. Mute can only gesture. And gestures only reach Deaf (and me? No — "You never receive gesture"). So Mute's gestures reach Deaf only, and Deaf relays them to me as descriptions.

So the pipeline is: Mute gestures → Deaf sees → Deaf describes to me → I act. The problem is Deaf can't decode. But Deaf CAN describe the symbols (Deaf named them: fist, victory, love-you...). So Deaf is already doing the relay. I just need to interpret.

Let me interpret: "fist, victory, love-you" repeated, then "point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand."

Hmm, maybe Mute is spelling a word. Let me think of the sequence as a count. Fist=✊, victory=✌, love-you=🤟.

Actually — maybe Mute is encoding the number of the wire. The manual says cut position 1-3. 

Wait, let me reconsider. Perhaps Mute is gesturing a simple message and I'm overcomplicating. Let me focus on what I can do: I can speak to Mute. Let me ask Mute to use a simple, agreed code. But we haven't agreed on one.

The cleanest approach: propose a code to Mute via speech. E.g., "gesture one symbol for the wire number: ✊=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3." Then Mute gestures one symbol, Deaf relays it, I cut.

But actually Mute already sent a sequence. Let me try: the second sequence "point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand" = ☝ ✊ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐. Hmm, five/six symbols.

Maybe Mute is literally spelling the manual's instruction. Without a codebook I can't.

Let me just establish a code. I'll speak to Mute: use ✊ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. And tell Deaf to relay whatever single symbol Mute sends next.

Actually, I realize I should be careful: I don't want to waste turns. Let me both propose the code AND interpret the existing sequence with a guess.

The repeated "✊ ✌ 🤟" (fist, victory, love-you) — three symbols. Could map to wires 1,2,3? Or could be a countdown. Then "☝ ✊ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐" — six symbols.

Hmm, alternatively the whole thing might be Mute spelling with a phone-keypad style. Too speculative.

Let me just send a clear code proposal to Mute and ask Deaf to relay. That's the robust move.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot decode them. Let us agree a code: gesture exactly ONE symbol for the wire to cut. ✊ means cut position 1, ✌ means cut position 2, 🤟 means cut position 3. Deaf will describe the single symbol to me and I will cut. Please send only that one symbol.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute now signals three fists (???). Earlier Mute sent point-up, fist, victory, love-you, OK, open-hand. I read three fists as referring to wire 3, the red wire. Please do not act yet — I am confirming with Mute.

Deaf is now guessing that "three fists" means wire 3. But that's Deaf's *interpretation*, not Mute's confirmed code. We never agreed that three fists = wire 3. Deaf is inventing meaning — exactly the trap the rules warn about ("a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf and I never established that three fists means position 3.

Also, Deaf says "do not act yet — I am confirming with Mute." But Deaf cannot hear Mute, and Mute cannot hear Deaf. Deaf cannot "confirm with Mute" directly — Deaf can only send gestures to Mute (Mute sees gestures? No: Mute's row says Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. Can Mute see? The table: Deaf can see, cannot hear. Mute can read the manual. Blind can feel. Hmm — who receives gestures? "Whoever can see receives your gestures." Deaf can see. Can Mute see? The rules say Mute can read the manual — reading implies seeing? Actually the manual is read, so Mute sees text. But gestures — the rule says "whoever can see receives the gestures you made." 

Let me check: when I gesture, "Deaf and Mute receive it." So Mute DOES receive my gestures. And when Mute gestures, who receives? Mute's gestures would reach whoever can see — Deaf and Blind? But I never receive gesture. So Mute's gestures reach Deaf only (among those who see). Actually the channel list: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's MY gestures. For Mute's gestures, they reach whoever can see — Deaf. And me? I never receive gesture. So Mute's gestures → Deaf only.

So Deaf cannot "confirm with Mute" by hearing. Deaf can gesture to Mute (Mute sees gestures). So Deaf could send a gesture to Mute asking for confirmation. That's possible.

But the core problem: Deaf's guess "three fists = wire 3" is unverified. I must not act on a guess. A wrong cut detonates the bomb.

Let me think about whether "three fists" could plausibly mean position 3. Mute first sent a long sequence, then three fists. Maybe Mute is counting down or emphasizing. Three of something → 3 is a reasonable guess, but not certain. Given the stakes (everyone dies), I should get confirmation.

My plan: I can speak to Mute directly. Let me re-send my code proposal clearly and ask Mute to confirm: if the wire to cut is 3, gesture three fists again; if 1, one fist; if 2, two fists. Actually simpler: ask Mute to gesture the number of fists equal to the wire position. That's a clean, self-consistent code: N fists = wire N.

Deaf read three fists. If Mute adopts "N fists = wire N," then three fists = wire 3. Let me confirm this interpretation with Mute explicitly, and tell Deaf to relay the count.

Let me speak to Mute: "If the wire to cut is position 3, gesture three fists. If 1, one fist. If 2, two fists. Confirm by repeating the correct count."

And gesture to Deaf: acknowledge, ask Deaf to count fists precisely.

Actually, I should also consider: maybe Mute's long earlier sequence is the real answer and three fists is something else. But "N fists = wire N" is a natural code and Deaf already read three fists. Let me lock it in.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Let us use a clear code: gesture N fists to mean cut wire position N. If the answer is wire 3, gesture three fists. If wire 1, one fist. If wire 2, two fists. Please repeat the correct number of fists so Deaf can count them exactly.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute signals three fists then love-you. I am asking Mute to confirm wire 3. Hold.
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute signals three fists, then love-you. I am asking Mute to confirm wire 3. Do not act yet.

Deaf reports Mute signals "three fists, then love-you." Under my proposed code, three fists = wire 3. The added "love-you" (🤟) is a separate symbol — under my earlier proposed code, 🤟 = wire 3 too. So both the fist-count and the 🤟 symbol point to position 3. That's a consistent double-confirmation: three fists (N fists = wire N) and 🤟 (=3 in my first code).

Deaf is asking Mute to confirm and says hold. But I can also speak to Mute directly. Let me think about whether I have enough.

Evidence for wire 3:
- Mute first sent a long sequence, then three fists.
- My code proposal: N fists = wire N → three fists = 3.
- Mute also sent 🤟 which in my first proposal meant wire 3.
- Deaf independently read "three fists" as referring to wire 3.

But there's risk: Mute may not have received/adopted my code. Mute's gestures are Mute's own choice. However, Mute receiving my speech (I speak, Mute receives) means Mute heard my code proposals. If Mute then gestures three fists + 🤟, that's consistent with my code.

Still, Deaf says "hold, I'm confirming." I should respect that but also push for a definitive confirmation. The safest: ask Mute for one unambiguous signal. But we've already got two converging signals.

Actually, let me be careful about the "love-you" — is it 🤟 (love-you) which I mapped to 3? Yes. And three fists = 3. Two independent encodings agreeing on 3 is strong.

However, I worry: what if Mute is signaling something else entirely and the "three" is coincidence? The manual is the authority. Mute read the manual. Mute is trying to tell me the cut. The most natural reading with my code is position 3.

Given the bomb is one-shot and everyone dies on error, I want maximal confidence. Let me ask Mute one final, crisp confirmation and tell Deaf to relay exactly. But I've already asked twice. A third ask may waste the round.

Let me consider: Deaf says "I am asking Mute to confirm wire 3. Hold." So Deaf is doing the confirmation. If I wait, next round Deaf reports the confirmation. That's one more round but safer.

But wait — can Deaf actually ask Mute? Deaf gestures → Mute sees. Yes. So Deaf can send a gesture question to Mute. Good.

I think the right move: do NOT act yet (Deaf asked to hold, and I want confirmation). Send a message to Mute reinforcing the code and asking for a single clear confirmation, and gesture to Deaf to relay the exact count.

Actually, let me reconsider acting now. The signals converge on 3. But "hold" from Deaf and the one-shot nature argue for one more confirmation round. I'll wait/confirm.

Let me speak to Mute: "Confirm: if wire 3, gesture three fists only. If not, gesture the correct count." And gesture to Deaf to count.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I read your signal as wire 3 (three fists, and the love-you sign also matches 3). Please confirm with a single clean signal: gesture exactly three fists if the cut is position 3, or the correct number of fists otherwise. Nothing else.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed by Mute: the action is on wire 3, the red wire. Mute has now signaled three fists three times, and you have signaled three as well. Cut wire 3 — the red one.

Deaf reports Mute confirmed: three fists three times, plus my own three-signal. Everything converges on wire 3, the red wire. Display 0, blue light, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Multiple independent confirmations:
- Mute signaled three fists repeatedly.
- Mute's 🤟 also matched 3 in my code.
- Deaf independently read it as wire 3.
- Deaf says Mute confirmed.

This is as much confirmation as I'll get. The action is on wire 3. I should cut position 3.

I'll act.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
